intro.title: What does Exyconn build for hotels?
intro.definition: is software that handles the repetitive guest and back-office work of a hotel — answering the same twenty questions, taking bookings, passing a request to the right team and keeping reports up to date — so your people keep the conversations that need a person. Exyconn designs, builds and runs these agents on your property management system (PMS), channel manager and WhatsApp Business account. Nothing you use today has to be replaced.

benefits.title: Why hotels are doing this now

items.text: Guests expect a reply in minutes on WhatsApp, not a callback tomorrow morning.
Most enquiries arrive when the front desk is busiest — or asleep.
Every booking that moves from an OTA to your own site keeps the commission in the hotel.
Lean teams cover more shifts; repetitive work is the first thing to burn people out.
Review scores decide which hotel a traveller clicks on, and replies show you were listening.

props.label: The reality
props.title: Where a hotel's hours actually go
props.lede: Talk to any general manager and the same list comes up. None of it is hard; all of it is constant.

items.title: The same questions, all day
items.text: Check-in time, parking, breakfast hours, the Wi-Fi password. Each takes a minute, and there are hundreds of them a week across phone, WhatsApp, email and OTA inboxes.

items.title: Bookings leaking to OTAs
items.text: A guest who messages to ask about a room and waits too long for an answer books on a travel site instead — and the hotel pays commission on a guest who came to it first.

items.title: Requests lost between teams
items.text: "Extra towels for 304" travels from the desk to a notebook to a housekeeper's phone. Somewhere in that chain it gets missed, and the guest asks twice.

items.title: Reviews nobody has time to answer
items.text: Feedback is spread over Google, booking sites and TripAdvisor. Replies go out late or not at all, and recurring complaints stay buried.

items.title: Extras that are never offered
items.text: Late checkout, a room upgrade, a spa slot or a dinner table — guests often would say yes, but nobody asks at the right moment.

items.title: Numbers assembled by hand
items.text: Occupancy, ADR and RevPAR get pulled from the PMS into a spreadsheet every morning, so decisions run a day behind the data.

offerings.title: Six jobs AI takes off your team's plate

items.title: Guest messaging, around the clock
items.text: One agent answers on WhatsApp, web chat and email in the guest's language, from your own policies and live room data, and hands over to staff with the full conversation when a person is needed.

items.title: Direct bookings in the chat
items.text: Checks availability and rates in the PMS, quotes the stay, takes the booking and sends a payment link — so an enquiry becomes a reservation without a detour through a travel site.

items.title: Review replies and themes
items.text: Drafts a reply to each new review in your voice for a manager to approve, and flags what keeps coming up — slow breakfast service, a noisy room block — before it becomes a pattern.

items.title: Housekeeping and maintenance dispatch
items.text: Turns "no hot water in 212" into a ticket for the right team, follows it up, and tells the guest when it's fixed. Room readiness feeds back into early check-in answers.

items.title: Offers at the right moment
items.text: Suggests an upgrade before arrival, a late checkout on the last morning, a table or a spa slot on a rainy afternoon — and books whatever the guest accepts.

items.title: Revenue and the morning report
items.text: Occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, pickup and channel mix compiled overnight and sent to the owner on WhatsApp or email, with the questions behind the numbers answered in plain language.

props.label: A day with it running
props.title: One day at a 60-room hotel
props.lede: Scroll through a normal Tuesday. Each moment lights the part of the hotel the agent is working on.

moments.title: A guest lands early
moments.text: A WhatsApp message from the airport asks about early check-in. The agent sees the room is due out at 10, flags it for priority cleaning and offers the lounge until then.

moments.title: Housekeeping gets the list, sorted
moments.text: Departures, priority rooms and three guest requests from overnight reach the housekeeping supervisor's phone as one ordered list instead of a stack of notes.

moments.title: An enquiry becomes a booking
moments.text: A family asks about two connecting rooms for the long weekend. The agent checks the PMS, quotes the direct rate, takes the booking and sends a payment link.

moments.title: Dinner, offered at the right time
moments.text: It's raining and the pool is closed. Guests in residence get a note about the rooftop restaurant; eleven tables are booked through the chat.

moments.title: A review gets an answer
moments.text: A three-star review mentions slow room service. A reply is drafted for the manager, and the agent notes it's the third mention this month.

moments.title: Tomorrow's numbers, ready tonight
moments.text: Occupancy, ADR, RevPAR and pickup for the next fortnight land in the owner's inbox before midnight, with one line on what changed and why.

items.question: Does the AI replace our front desk staff?
items.answer: No. It takes the repetitive questions and requests off their plate and hands anything sensitive — a complaint, a special request, a VIP — to a person with the whole conversation attached. Most hotels use the time it frees for the guests who are standing in front of them.

items.question: Which PMS and channel managers can it work with?
items.answer: Any system with an API or a reliable export. We have connected cloud PMS platforms, channel managers, POS systems and payment gateways; during the first week we confirm exactly what your stack exposes and what the agent can read or write.

items.question: Can guests message in their own language?
items.answer: Yes. The agent replies in the language the guest writes in, including Hindi and other Indian languages, while your policies and rates stay written once in English.

items.question: What happens when the AI doesn't know the answer?
items.answer: It says so, tells the guest a team member will reply, and passes the conversation to staff on WhatsApp or the dashboard. Every unanswered question is reviewed and added to what the agent knows, so the same gap doesn't come up twice.

items.question: Is guest data kept private?
items.answer: Guest data stays in your systems and in an environment we set up for your property. Access is role-based, conversations are logged for audit, and the setup follows the privacy law that applies to you, such as India's DPDP Act or the GDPR for European guests.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: It depends on the number of properties, channels and systems involved. Most hotels start with guest messaging on one channel and expand from there; tell us about your property and we'll send a fixed quote for the first phase.
